name: Eiffel Tower
hook: A despised iron eyesore that became Paris — and Jeopardy asks about the criticism, the rivets and the height.

facts.label: the 1889 Universal Exposition
facts.statement: The tower was built for the 1889 Universal Exposition and honored the 100th anniversary of the French Revolution.

facts.label: wrought iron
facts.statement: It is made of about 7,000 tons of iron: 18,038 pieces joined by 2.5 million rivets.

facts.label: world's tallest structure
facts.statement: It was the world's tallest structure until the Chrysler Building surpassed it in 1930; before the tower, the Washington Monument held the title.

facts.label: Paris and the Seine
facts.statement: It stands in Paris on the Seine; the grassy Champ de Mars opposite it is named for the Roman god of war.

facts.label: the artists' petition
facts.statement: De Maupassant, Zola and Dumas fils were among those who signed a petition decrying it as "a gigantic factory chimney."

facts.label: its antennas
facts.statement: Antennas raised the tower's height from 984 to 1,052 feet in 1957; a 1953 TV antenna had added about 70 feet.

facts.label: Franz Reichelt
facts.statement: Tailor Franz Reichelt died around 1911 jumping from the Eiffel Tower to test a combination suit and parachute he invented.
